get.description: Whether the import is set up on this server, the caller's own connection with the mailbox's address, and the partner's connection without it. Nothing is asked of Google.

delete.description: Asks Google to withdraw the permission (if Google cannot be reached, the rest still happens) and removes the caller's own connection with its token. Disconnecting again changes nothing. The partner's connection is never touched.

post.description: Makes a ticket that is good for ten minutes, once, in this browser (it is bound to it by a cookie that is sent with this answer), and answers with Google's address to send the browser to. Google asks for read-only access to Gmail and nothing else, and sends the browser back to the server, which ends on the web app's e-mail page. Answers mail-not-set-up while the import is off.

get.description: Answers without a sign-in and always with a redirect to the web app's e-mail page: `connected=yes` when the mailbox was connected, `refused` when the person said no at Google, `failed` for everything else. It accepts nothing but a ticket the server issued, once, in time, from the browser it was issued to. Not for clients of the API: only browsers coming from Google.

303.description: To the e-mail page, whatever happened.

get.summary: Where Google sends the browser back to

parameters.description: Which suggestions: the ones that wait (the default), the accepted or the rejected ones, or ALL.

post.description: Makes what it proposes (or what the body says) and answers with the suggestion, which now names what was made. Accepting again answers the same and makes nothing more. A suggestion that was rejected answers already-decided. What would be made is checked like adding by hand: if it is not valid the answer lists the fields, nothing is made and the suggestion still waits.
Makes nothing. Rejecting again answers the same; a suggestion that was accepted answers already-decided.
